query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of W-Cu composites produced by spark-plasma sintering and conventional induction or arc-plasma casting
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity and mechanical strength of the spark-plasma sintered W-Cu composite are not significantly higher than those of the conventionally cast composite, the hypothesis is falsified. Significance is defined as a 10% increase in thermal conductivity and a 5% increase in mechanical strength.

cited_evidence.text: The unique design concept of HEAs can be applied to the innovation of a new generation of powder superalloys and the development of turbine disk components suitable for the extreme working conditions of the aero-engine. Combining MA (mechanical alloying) with SPS (spark plasma sintering) to prepare HEAs has recently received much attention. MA overcomes phase diagram limitations by using mechanical energy to effect the atomic alloying of solid components, producing alloy systems inaccessible to conventional procedures and increasing powder homogeneity and solid solubility. SPS is a new rapid sintering technology commonly used to prepare high-performance HEA blocks. It combines plasma activation and hot-pressing sintering and benefits from fast heating and cooling rates, short sintering times, controllable microstructures, energy savings, and low environmental impact. Pulse current heating and high pressure can rapidly heat and sinter the powder particles into sintered blocks [,,]. However, many challenges remain in preparing HEAs using MA and SPS, such as the selection of initial elements, setting of milling parameters, selecting process control agents (PCAs), and controlling the s

The presence of the second phase (Fm3̅m) may also have an effect on the transport properties. Its investigation would be useful to reach a single-phase system through the adjustment of SPS parameters and obtain a comparison of the TE properties between multiphase and single-phase systems. Further doping or alteration of the composition is planned to increase the yield and achieve the p-type behavior of the semiconductor material.

However, due to the high melting points of the refractory elements utilized in these HEAs, incomplete melting and chemical heterogeneity [], as well as casting defects and a coarse microstructure [,] may develop in the alloys. In addition, the processing route may not be compatible with industrial processes due to the high cost of equipment and limitations in product shape and size []. Powder metallurgy (PM) is advantageous due to its near-net shape capability and competence in the processing of refractory and other elements with different densities [,,,] to minimize evaporation of low-melting point elements. The PM process can also produce non-equilibrium phases, and a more homogenous and nanocrystalline grain structure [,]. Some recent studies demonstrated that the mechanical properties of PM-processed refractory HEAs were at least at par or superior to those obtained by ingot metallurgy [,,]. However, only a handful of studies have investigated the electrochemical properties of these biomedical PM-processed HEAs.
